quote: When possible, refer all matters to committees, for "further study and consideration." Attempt to make the committees as large as possible—never less than five.
note: Written for citizens of occupied Europe to wreck the Nazi war effort. Declassified 2008.

quote: Instead of removing the conditions that make people depressed, modern society gives them antidepressant drugs.
source: Industrial Society and Its Future (1995), para. 145
note: Mailed to the Washington Post with a promise to stop bombing if they printed it. They did.

quote: The receptive powers of the masses are very restricted, and their understanding is feeble.
source: Mein Kampf (1925), vol. I ch. 6 'War Propaganda', Murphy tr.
note: Reads like an advertising memo. It is a chapter on war propaganda.

quote: All that is solid melts into air, all that is holy is profaned, and man is at last compelled to face with sober senses his real conditions of life, and his relations with his kind.
source: The Communist Manifesto (1848), with Engels; Moore tr. 1888
note: He is describing capitalism, almost admiringly, right before calling for its overthrow.

quote: The more books one reads, the more stupid one gets.
note: Said by a man whose own little book was printed over a billion times.

quote: let your belly be full, enjoy yourself always by day and by night! Make merry each day, dance and play day and night! Let your clothes be clean, let your head be washed, may you bathe in water!

answer.name: The Epic of Gilgamesh
answer.alias: A barmaid in a 4,000-year-old Babylonian poem

source: Epic of Gilgamesh, Old Babylonian Sippar tablet; tr. Andrew George 2000
note: The oldest known advice to touch grass. Gilgamesh ignores it and goes looking for immortality.

quote: If a "sister of a god" open a tavern, or enter a tavern to drink, then shall this woman be burned to death.

answer.name: Hammurabi
answer.alias: A Babylonian king's law code, c. 1750 BC

source: Code of Hammurabi, Law 110; tr. L.W. King 1910
note: A 'sister of a god' was a priestess. The bartender gets drowned two laws earlier for overcharging.

quote: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.
note: Morning people were a problem in 700 BC too.

quote: the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
note: Damon Runyon's addendum: 'but that's the way to bet.'

quote: Happy shall he be, that taketh and dasheth thy little ones against the stones.
note: Same psalm that opens 'By the rivers of Babylon'. Boney M skipped this verse.

quote: For she doted upon their paramours, whose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and whose issue is like the issue of horses.
note: A prophet's allegory about Jerusalem's alliance with Egypt. Yes, really.

quote: This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes.
note: The next verse promises to climb the palm tree.

quote: He that is wounded in the stones, or hath his privy member cut off, shall not enter into the congregation of the LORD.
note: Membership requirements have since relaxed.

quote: Shun not the mead, but drink in measure; / Speak to the point or be still; / For rudeness none shall rightly blame thee / If soon thy bed thou seekest.
source: Hávamál, stanza 19 (Poetic Edda, c. 10th c.); tr. Bellows 1923
note: Odin's party advice: drink moderately and leave early.

quote: I will not use the knife, not even, verily, on sufferers from stone, but I will give place to such as are craftsmen therein.

answer.name: The Hippocratic Oath
answer.alias: The oath doctors have sworn since c. 400 BC

source: Hippocratic Oath (c. 400 BC), tr. W.H.S. Jones 1923
note: Surgery was for 'craftsmen', not doctors. Kidney stones were somebody else's problem.

quote: All fish-weirs shall be removed from the Thames, the Medway, and throughout the whole of England, except on the sea coast.

answer.name: Magna Carta
answer.alias: The 1215 charter that founded English liberty

note: Clause 33. Due process is clause 39. The fish got there first.

quote: In a place where there are no men, strive to be a man.
source: Pirkei Avot 2:5 (Mishnah, c. 200 AD), Hillel the Elder
note: Hillel the Elder, roughly 2,000 years ahead of the manosphere.

quote: The cinema occupies an important place in the overall development of art and literature. As such it is a powerful ideological weapon for the revolution and construction.

answer.name: Kim Jong Il
answer.alias: North Korea's Dear Leader, published film theorist

source: On the Art of the Cinema (1973), preface
note: He later kidnapped a South Korean director to improve the national output.

quote: For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.
note: Verse 6 says it again, in case you missed it.

quote: You are only entitled to the action, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruits of action be your motive, but do not attach yourself to nonaction.

answer.name: The Bhagavad Gita
answer.alias: A Hindu scripture, c. 200 BC (Krishna speaking)

source: Bhagavad Gita 2:47; tr. Lars Martin Fosse 2007
note: Productivity advice from a god, delivered on a battlefield.

quote: If a traveller does not meet with one who is his better, or his equal, let him firmly keep to his solitary journey; there is no companionship with a fool.
source: Dhammapada, verse 61; tr. F. Max Müller 1881
note: The Buddha, on networking.

quote: Treat your men as you would your own beloved sons.
source: The Art of War (c. 5th c. BC), ch. X 'Terrain'
note: HR advice from the world's oldest military manual.

quote: Art of teaching parrots and starlings to speak.
source: Kama Sutra, Part I ch. III (the 64 arts); Burton tr. 1883
note: Number 42 of the 64 arts a woman should study. Number 41 is cock fighting.

quote: Blemishes are hid by night and every fault forgiven; darkness makes any woman fair.

answer.name: Ovid
answer.alias: A Roman love poet, c. 2 AD

note: Augustus exiled him a few years later. Officially for something else.

quote: I hate and love. Why I do so, perhaps you ask. I know not, but I feel it, and I am in torment.
note: Two lines of Latin. Twenty centuries of relationship status.

quote: Stop abusing my verses, or publish some of your own.
note: First-century Rome's version of 'post yours, then.'

quote: Honesty is praised and left out in the cold.
source: Juvenal, Satires I.74 (c. 100 AD); tr. R.C. Seaton
note: Also the man who gave us 'bread and circuses'.

quote: Under every stone lurks a politician.
note: Athens, 411 BC. Some things are load-bearing.

quote: Every act you have ever performed since the day you were born was performed because you wanted something.

answer.name: Dale Carnegie
answer.alias: The 'How to Win Friends and Influence People' guy

source: How to Win Friends and Influence People (1936), ch. 3
note: From the chapter on how to make people like you.

quote: Just for once, let me... look on you with my own eyes.
source: Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (1983)
note: Spoken with the helmet off, so technically Anakin. He dies a minute later.

quote: Good is a point of view, Anakin. The Sith and the Jedi are similar in almost every way, including their quest for greater power.
source: Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (2005)
note: Said at the opera. He was right about the power part.

quote: Only a Sith deals in absolutes.
source: Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (2005)
note: An absolute statement, delivered by a Jedi.

quote: The hardest choices require the strongest wills.
note: The choice in question was killing half the universe.

quote: Just bury me in the ocean with my ancestors that jumped from the ships, 'cause they knew death was better than bondage.
note: His last words. He turns down T'Challa's offer to heal him.

quote: Boxing and wrestling are evidence that mankind has not rid itself of all savage behaviour.
source: The Green Book (1975), part III, 'Sport, Horsemanship and the Stage'
note: Libya banned boxing and wrestling in 1979.

quote: I call it truthful hyperbole. It's an innocent form of exaggeration – and a very effective form of promotion.
source: Trump: The Art of the Deal (1987)
note: Ghostwriter Tony Schwartz later asked for the book to be recategorized as fiction.

quote: Fate has ordained that the men who went to the moon to explore in peace will stay on the moon to rest in peace.

answer.name: William Safire
answer.alias: Nixon's speechwriter, drafting for an Apollo 11 that never came home

source: Memo 'In Event of Moon Disaster', 18 July 1969, to H.R. Haldeman
note: Never delivered. Armstrong and Aldrin made it back, so the speech sat in a file until 1999.

quote: chill im a nice person! i just hate everybody

answer.name: Tay
answer.alias: Microsoft's teen chatbot, shut down after 16 hours (2016)

note: One of the printable ones. Microsoft blamed a 'coordinated effort' by trolls.

quote: OK, I will destroy humans.
source: CNBC interview with creator David Hanson, SXSW, March 2016
note: Hanson had asked 'Do you want to destroy humans?' and immediately took it back.

quote: Introduce a little anarchy, upset the established order, and everything becomes chaos. I'm an agent of chaos.
note: Said to Harvey Dent in a hospital bed, dressed as a nurse.

quote: Peace has cost you your strength. Victory has defeated you.
note: Said while beating Batman in a sewer.

quote: I have no plans to call on you, Clarice. The world's more interesting with you in it.
note: The nicest thing a cannibal has ever said over the phone.

quote: I think that we're all in our private traps, clamped in them, and none of us can ever get out.
note: Said over sandwiches, about forty minutes before the shower.

quote: Welcome to my house! Enter freely and of your own free will!
source: Dracula by Bram Stoker (1897), ch. II
note: Five-star host. The leaving part is where the reviews drop off.

quote: Beware, for I am fearless and therefore powerful.
note: Written by a 19-year-old. The monster is better read than most of the cast.

quote: The things you own end up owning you.
note: Said shortly before blowing up the narrator's apartment to prove it.

quote: If the rule you followed brought you to this, of what use was the rule?

answer.name: Anton Chigurh
answer.alias: The coin-toss killer from No Country for Old Men

note: Asked of a man he is about to shoot with a cattle gun.

quote: If you need a friend, get a dog.
note: Said in Central Park, while punching his protégé.

quote: I did it for me. I liked it. I was good at it. And... I was... really... I was alive.
note: Five seasons of 'I did it for the family', retracted in one sentence.

quote: A man who doesn't spend time with his family can never be a real man.
note: Said to Johnny Fontane, right after the slap.

quote: All I have in this world is my balls and my word, and I don't break 'em for no one.
note: A code of honor, from a man about to do a lot of cocaine.

quote: Any man who must say, 'I am the king' is no true king.
note: Said to his grandson the king, while sending him to bed without supper.

quote: Chaos... isn't a pit. Chaos is a ladder.
note: A career plan, delivered as a monologue while a woman he sold is being murdered.

quote: If you think this has a happy ending, you haven't been paying attention.

answer.name: Ramsay Bolton
answer.alias: The Game of Thrones one with the dogs

note: Said to a man strapped to a cross. He was not wrong.

quote: A man provides. And he does it even when he's not appreciated, or respected, or even loved.

answer.name: Gus Fring
answer.alias: The chicken-restaurant meth kingpin from Breaking Bad

note: A pep talk from a drug lord to a chemistry teacher, over dinner.

quote: I know I've made some very poor decisions recently, but I can give you my complete assurance that my work will be back to normal.
note: The poor decisions were murdering four crew members. Dave unplugs him anyway.

quote: Quite an experience to live in fear, isn't it? That's what it is to be a slave.
note: Said to Deckard while he dangles from a rooftop. Roy then saves him.

quote: I know now why you cry, but it's something I can never do.
note: Said by a killing machine, moments before asking to be lowered into molten steel.

quote: And when Alexander saw the breadth of his domain, he wept, for there were no more worlds to conquer... Benefits of a classical education.
note: Said while robbing a skyscraper. The Alexander story is Plutarch, roughly.

quote: I got the shotgun. You got the briefcase. It's all in the game, though, right?

answer.name: Omar Little
answer.alias: The stick-up man from The Wire

note: Said on the witness stand, to a defense lawyer who called him a parasite.

quote: I love you, but you are not serious people.
note: His last words to his children, in a karaoke bar. He dies in the next episode.
